note: Dated-claim register. Tearline is a developer library, not a regulated product, so it makes almost no claims about the world that decay on a calendar. What it claims is that external artefacts exist and are reachable. All three availability claims were re-fetched on 2026-07-31 and every value held — nothing drifted, and no page copy needed changing. On 2026-07-31 a third page (/dom-to-png) shipped, and it is the first surface on this host that quotes numbers about OTHER software: four npm packages' versions, licences, dependency counts, publish dates and sizes. Those are exactly the kind of value that goes stale invisibly, so each package is now its own register entry and the page prints the fetch date beside every figure. Every entry was fetched on its lastVerified date; none is remembered.

claims.claim: Whether Tearline's source is readable on GitHub, and where the MIT licence can be verified

claims.note: Re-checked 2026-07-29: `gh repo view kyisaiah47/tearline` reports visibility PRIVATE and an anonymous GET of the repo URL returns HTTP 404. Every GitHub link was REMOVED on 2026-07-29 — the header's GitHub CTA now points at the on-origin playground, the hero's "MIT - zero dependencies" badge points at opensource.org/license/mit, and the footer's GitHub row is replaced by "Read the source" -> /tearline.js, which is the entire 340-line unminified component and makes the source claim literally true while the repo stays private. package.json's repository field is left as-is: it is package metadata, not a claim rendered to a buyer. Re-checked 2026-07-30: an anonymous GET of the repo URL still returns HTTP 404, so the repository is still private and every removal from 2026-07-29 still stands. This is also the measured reason github.com out-cites us on Tearline's own queries — engines answering "html to receipt image javascript" cite readable repositories, and ours cannot be read. Flipping it public is the single highest-leverage act available on this product, and it is not a page we can write. Re-checked 2026-07-31: `gh repo view kyisaiah47/tearline --json visibility` returns {"visibility":"PRIVATE"} and an anonymous GET still returns HTTP 404. Every removal from 2026-07-29 still stands. github.com remains the top competitor-gap domain on this product's queries for exactly this reason, and it is still not a gap a page can close — /dom-to-png, shipped 2026-07-31, answers the same questions on-origin instead, but a readable repo would outrank it.

claims.note: Fetched from MDN on 2026-07-31; the wording on the page is a paraphrase of the 'Security and tainted canvases' section, not a quote.
